subject: Need for more graphical control and upload/download

messages.author: 5c62f141ff72ee02
messages.subject: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
parts:
Just set Shiny up on my pharmacogenomics group's R-studio server here at Mayo clinic. Love it. I've set it up to generate fairly detailed reactive plots for any genes of interest, and am curious to see how well those with less computational expertise take to it.

Two initial comments though:

1. It would be good to have more control over graphics dimensions. I see this has already come up in another posting. I feel more can be done. When running Shiny on data like mine (tens of thousands of genes) a plot for any gene may have 1 feature or it may have 50 features. It all depends on the amount of data for the gene. Normally I have my output dimensions be some multiple of feature number (e.g. height=feature_number*100). There doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way to do this in Shiny. There also doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way of controlling the ability to scroll images.

2. I see Shiny being really useful in groups like mine where there is far too much data and team members want a way to visualise a lot and then trim down to easily manageable data for their own analysis. Allowing me to get on with my own research without many low-level requests! It would be good to have an upload and download feature. Where standardised data formats can be uploaded, merged with the greater set of data, analysis run and results returned. Also any results from the reactive plot exploration downloaded (e.g. CSV of top features for a gene).

Great work so far,
Quin
P.S. Please keep the production quality server version free, and focus on charging for a hosting and support service!

messages.author: f806781d102fe0ab
messages.subject: Re: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
parts: 1. It would be good to have more control over graphics dimensions. I see this has already come up in another posting. I feel more can be done. When running Shiny on data like mine (tens of thousands of genes) a plot for any gene may have 1 feature or it may have 50 features. It all depends on the amount of data for the gene. Normally I have my output dimensions be some multiple of feature number (e.g. height=feature_number*100). There doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way to do this in Shiny. There also doesn't seem to be a fuss-free way of controlling the ability to scroll images.

Good suggestion--I'm about to check in a change that lets you use a function to specify the width and/or height. The function can refer to reactive inputs and functions. This way if you have your data subset saved as a reactive function, you can define the width/height in terms of that data and it will automatically resize/redraw the graph.

I'm not sure what the right answer is for scrolling right now. I was tempted to add a generic scrollPanel but I don't think it makes that much sense in light of the way our current "template" (pageWithSidebar) works--I think we need a template that is more app-like and less page-like.

2. I see Shiny being really useful in groups like mine where there is far too much data and team members want a way to visualise a lot and then trim down to easily manageable data for their own analysis. Allowing me to get on with my own research without many low-level requests! It would be good to have an upload and download feature. Where standardised data formats can be uploaded, merged with the greater set of data, analysis run and results returned. Also any results from the reactive plot exploration downloaded (e.g. CSV of top features for a gene).

There is a sort of half-baked input feature which is fileInput. The main limitations are that it only works with very recent versions of Chrome, Safari, and Firefox, and it doesn't show progress. But it should mostly work. I'm working on the download feature, most of the plumbing is done but I'm still working on what the functions should look like.
P.S. Please keep the production quality server version free, and focus on charging for a hosting and support service!

The feedback we've heard so far is that corporations mostly want server software, and it's mostly individuals and people in academia who want the hosting service. We're thinking hard about our business model, stay tuned...

messages.subject: Re: Need for more graphical control and upload/download
parts:
Great to hear, Joe. I look forward to seeing the progress. I demo'ed my Shiny genomics app to the team today and it was extremely well received.

I think you may be surprised about what people want. I've hosted my own commercial analysis software (all R/S+ back end). 5 years ago everybody wanted to bring servers in-house for security reasons but software as service is pretty standard these days... if you can assure basic data protection. For my company tying in R analysis web services with flexible e-commerce features was also key for customer-facing applications. I'm sure given enough time all these good things will come to Shiny ;)

Good luck!
Quin

Normally to get the very latest changes from GitHub you would need to have the devtools package installed and do devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

But in this particular case I just happened to rev the Shiny package yesterday so you can follow the normal instructions for installing the package on http://rstudio.com/shiny.
